content: We need a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction: the forward reaction is carbonyl-ene, so retrosynthetic step is the reverse: break a C-C bond formed in ene, generate a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene with allylic hydrogen. So we need to find a template that corresponds to carbonyl-ene reverse (i.e., an ene reaction). Likely template ID exists. We can search for templates that break a C-O bond (forming OH) and a C=C to give C=O and C=C? Actually forward: carbonyl-ene: carbonyl + alkene -> new C-C bond, new C-O (hydroxyl). So reverse: from product (hydroxy-alkyl) to carbonyl + alkene. So we need a template that breaks C-O (hydroxyl) and C-C (new bond) and forms C=O and C=C. Use search with functional_groups_broken: aliphatic hydroxyls, five-membered rings? The product has a five-membered ring (cyclopentanol). So broken: aliphatic hydroxyls, five-membered rings. Formed: ketones, C-C double bonds. Bonds broken: C-O, C-C (the bond formed in forward). Bonds formed: C=O, C=C. Need correct bond format: e.g., "6-8". But we don't know atom indices. Maybe we can omit bonds criteria and just search by functional groups. Let's try search with broken: aliphatic hydroxyls, five-membered rings; formed: ketones, C-C double bonds.
